examples.solution_text:
The region under the graph is a triangle with base $6$ s and height $8$ m/s.

$\begin{aligned}d&=\frac12\times6\times8\\&=24\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

For each runner, add the accelerating triangle, cruising rectangle and braking triangle. Runner A cruises for $8-3=5$ seconds; runner B cruises for $8-4=4$ seconds. Both brake for $12-8=4$ seconds.

$\begin{aligned}d_A&=\frac12\times3\times8+5\times8+\frac12\times4\times8\\&=12+40+16\\&=68\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}d_B&=\frac12\times4\times6+4\times6+\frac12\times4\times6\\&=12+24+12\\&=48\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

Runner A travels further by $68-48=20\text{ m}$.

coverage.summary: Authored five worked examples covering all distinct assessed area methods and duration/comparison steps, using changed source values. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. Solutions retain editable prose and single-dollar aligned mathematics; TheoryView supplies blue solution ink. Graphs use standard semantic colours, black axes and labels, 10 pt ordinary labels and 8.5 pt ticks. Area partitions appear only in solutions. No source gaps; independent example review and actual visual capture remain later stages.

examples.derivation: The graph encloses a triangle: distance = (1/2) × 6 × 8 = 24 m. This follows Development Q5(c)'s deceleration-to-rest area method.
Cruising lasts 16 − 6 = 10 s. The accelerating triangle contributes (1/2) × 6 × 12 = 36 m; the rectangle contributes 10 × 12 = 120 m. Total distance = 156 m, following Development Q6(b).
Stage durations are 5 s, 12 − 5 = 7 s and 18 − 12 = 6 s. Areas are 45 m, 126 m and 54 m, giving 225 m. The three-stage partition matches the source distance example and Development Q7.

The lower-speed rectangle contributes 6 × 4 = 24 m. The speed difference is 10 − 4 = 6 m/s, so the triangle contributes (1/2) × 6 × 6 = 18 m. Total distance = 42 m. This uses the source's rectangle-plus-triangle decomposition; the decreasing-speed guidance preserves the same method.
Runner A's areas are 12 + 40 + 16 = 68 m. Runner B's areas are 12 + 24 + 12 = 48 m. Runner A travels 68 − 48 = 20 m further. Calculating both graph areas and subtracting follows Development Q7(a–c).
